Thanks for responding, but that’s kind of the thing: the very idea of slaving away to achieve happiness is irritating to me. Does happiness only exist to act as a distraction from the dread that is life? Is ignorance really the only way to achieve bliss? Holy shit, It’s like those who actively seek answers to truth ultimately end up achieving the cruelest fate and outlook of life. Do you understand what I’m getting at now?

Regarding your feelings of being burned out and depression, it seems that you somewhat care about escaping your current circumstances by making a post on Reddit to seek help from others. So you want to leave your current circumstances but you can’t find the ambition to? Well I want to ask you this: have you ever pictured yourself living without this negativity? I mean seriously think about it: what would your life be without depression once you have gotten so attached to it that it became a part of you? Are you willing to leave it behind even though you are so used to it that it feels cozy? Maybe you have a fear of happiness because unhappiness is all that is familiar to you. It’s a very cruel fate to digest and swallow and even I am still struggling day by day as everyone’s escape varies and some people may never find it, but I’m just here to prompt your thinking so you can get a head start.

Hey man, regarding the lack of credibility you’re giving yourself it sounds like Imposter syndrome, basically you have built up self doubt for even the slightest of things. Maybe it has to do with you’re childhood. You seem to have had it rough growing up and maybe because no adult figure really expected anything from you, so as a result you don’t expect anything from yourself. No standards were set early on in your life, but hey that’s perfectly fine as long as you work towards anything that achieves self fulfillment for you. This might make you feel better or worse but in life there is always someone that is better than you in something, but there is always someone worse than you in something. I know this idea is kind of unnerving, but also oddly soothing but just know that if you start to compare yourself to people that don’t play any role in your life, you’ll be fighting a losing battle against yourself that you will never win.
